deviation_out_of_scope_resolutions.disposition: Recorded as a deviation, not a D-08 finding: this is out of plan 02-03's declared file scope (predecessor_state named it out of scope), touched only because Task 2's own commit step is unreachable otherwise. Per D-06, this stage is a review instrument re-validated against the pinned tree before any corrective commit (D-06a) -- these 141 resolutions carry no independent authority and are not claimed as SYNC-02/PRES-02 evidence themselves.

packaging_and_ci_docs.decision: D-08 literally: 'a definition present on both sides, upstream's version wins outright.' These 20 paths (plugin marketplace/packaging config, CI workflow, skill markdown/scripts) are not AST-decomposable the way Python modules are, so the same rule is applied at whole-file granularity, treating the path itself as the shared 'definition' identity: 19 of 20 exist with real, differing content on both fork and upstream (verified via `git show <oid>:<path>` on both sides before resolving) and take upstream's file verbatim; skills/tooluniverse/REFERENCE.md exists only upstream (fork deleted it) and is restored from upstream, which is not a fork-content-loss risk since fork has no content to lose there.

deviation_out_of_scope_resolutions.reason: Task 2's <verify> requires `git status --porcelain` empty after commit, which is mechanically impossible while any of the 141 out-of-plan-scope paths (symlink_workspaces, packaging, ci_docs) remain conflicted -- git refuses to commit with any unmerged path present, regardless of task boundaries. Resolved under Rule 3 (blocking issue) with explicit, uniform, non-content-judgment rules distinct from Task 1/2's definition-level D-08 resolutions, so this array stays separable from the source-layer `resolutions` array's own counts.

symlink_workspaces.decision: git had already auto-resolved every one of these 114 conflicts at the path level (`D <name>` deleting the fork's symlink, `A <name>/...` adding upstream's materialized directory content) before this run began -- confirmed via `git status --porcelain -- 'plugin/skills/'` showing 528 A / 114 D. The only remaining unmerged artifact per symlink was git's own `<name>~HEAD` conflict-marker path (mode 120000, the fork's symlink object, preserved so it is not silently discarded). `git rm` on each `~HEAD` marker accepts git's own already-staged resolution (upstream's materialized directory) without opening, reading, or writing through any `plugin/skills/*` symlink -- the prohibition's literal text.

discovered_findings.description: llm_clients.py was NEVER part of conflicts_raw (285) -- git's own 3-way auto-merge (inside `git merge --no-commit --no-ff` in plan 02-02's Task 2) resolved it with zero conflict markers, yet silently dropped upstream's entire `AzureOpenAIClient` class (49 lines) from the result. Confirmed: class present at both fork_oid (no -- fork never had it) and upstream_oid (yes), absent from the auto-merged stage file before this plan's Task 3 fix. This blocked `generate_tools.main()`, which imports it transitively via agentic_tool.py (resolved to upstream's canonical version in Task 1, which does `from .llm_clients import AzureOpenAIClient`).
discovered_findings.fix: Applied resolve_source_module_conflict() (the same D-08 definition-level function used for Task 1's 16 flagged source modules) directly to llm_clients.py despite it never being flagged as conflicted -- fork_only_retained=[OllamaClient, ClaudeCliClient, ...], shared_taken_from_upstream=[BaseLLMClient, GeminiClient, OpenRouterClient, VLLMClient], upstream_only_added=[AzureOpenAIClient, OpenAICompatibleClient, ...]. resolved_name_set_matches_expected=true, fork_only_dropped=[].
discovered_findings.root_cause: git's textual 3-way merge for llm_clients.py treated the class additions on both sides (fork added OllamaClient/ClaudeCliClient; upstream added AzureOpenAIClient/OpenAICompatibleClient) as non-conflicting insertions at different file offsets, but its context-line diff heuristic silently dropped the AzureOpenAIClient hunk during the merge -- a genuine git auto-merge data-loss bug, not a mistake in either side's source or in this plan's resolution work.

discovered_findings.carried_to: 02-04 findings.json, expected disposition self_healed_downstream per D-06a (pinned tree already has it)
discovered_findings.description: Task 3's hard gate initially failed: test_json_type_fields_exist_in_lazy_registry found 3 unknown 'type' values (api_key, endpoint, secret) sourced from src/tooluniverse/data/api_keys_catalog.json -- a credential-metadata catalog, not a tool-definitions file, that _load_type_names()/_load_defined_tool_names() scan unconditionally.
discovered_findings.fix: Applied the identical 2-line guard (byte-for-byte, sourced from the current docs/gsd-codebase-map tree, not invented) to the stage's test file so Task 3's hard gate measures the real registration chain rather than this known, already-fixed test-scope gap. This is squarely self-healed-downstream territory per D-06a; recorded here rather than silently applied because it is genuinely outside D-08's mechanical rule.
discovered_findings.root_cause: Both fork@e0755067 and upstream@56adcfd9's pre-merge versions of this test lack an `if jf.name == "api_keys_catalog.json": continue` guard (verified: absent from both sides' test file, confirmed via `git show <oid>:tests/unit/test_registry_integrity.py`). `git blame` attributes the guard's 2 occurrences in the CURRENT docs/gsd-codebase-map tree to commit f81448f2 itself -- meaning whoever resolved the original merge's test_registry_integrity.py conflict added this guard as original authored content, not derived from either input side. D-08's definition-level rule has no provision for de novo human insight added during conflict resolution, so a faithful mechanical re-derivation correctly does not reproduce it.

added_from_upstream: # Benchmark harness — dev-only, kept locally but never tracked.
# Plugin build doesn't include skills/evals/ in dist, and .gitattributes
# already excludes it from `git archive` release tarballs.
# directories hold with-skill-vs-without-skill comparison runs produced
# by the skill evaluator. They have no SKILL.md (not real skills), match
# the sync-skills.sh `tooluniverse-*` glob accidentally, and bloat plugin/
# without ever shipping to users. Keep locally for dev, never track.
# One-off outputs from working-example scripts that write to cwd
# (e.g. ddi_working_example.py). Outputs should go to /tmp or an explicit
# Superseded skill source — when SKILL.md is rewritten, keep the prior
# version in git history (git log / git show) instead of beside the new
# one as SKILL_OLD.md, where it ships to users and causes confusion.
# Dev iteration notes that lived inside skill source: comparison
# write-ups, test feedback diaries, "fixed" twin implementations.
# Belong in git history or PR descriptions, not the shipped skill tree.
# Local-only harness sweep artifacts (test-all command output)
